newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy market watchdog questions Cirio.
newsitem.headline: Italy market watchdog questions Cirio.

text.p: The chairman of Italian food company Cirio has been given three days by stock market regulatory body Consob to answer questions on the activities of his companies.
Sources at Consob said Sergio Cragnotti had been told to make public his answers to a list of 22 questions in a statement that has to be published in a daily newspaper.
Cragnotti has the option of asking Consob to reconsider its decision, which could delay the process by a number of days, the sources said.

Consob summoned Cragnotti after the businessman announced he was transferring control of loss-making Serie A football club Lazio to Cirio from his own Luxembourg-based holding company Cragnotti & Partners. Cragnotti exercises a controlling interest in Cirio through a company called Sagrit, which in turn holds a dominant stake in Cirio.
Cragnotti caused an outcry among Italian institutional investors when it emerged Lazio would be sold to Cirio for 85 billion lire, well above its book value in Cragotti & Partners accounts.
